problem:
A function $f(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| $x$ | $0.7$ | $0.8$ | $0.9$ | $1.0$ | $1.1$ | $1.2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $13$ | $15$ | $18$ | $20$ | $22$ | $25$ |

Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=1.2$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

$\,\,{f}^{′}(1.2)≈$ {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h}
$$

 

at the point $x=1.2.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case, $h=0.1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1.2) & ≈\frac{f(1.2)-f(1.2-0.1)}{0.1} \\  & =\frac{f(1.2)-f(1.1)}{0.1} \\  & =\frac{25-22}{0.1} \\  & =\frac{3}{0.1} \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$
